narrative.overview: AI Canva is a working transit system for ideas. Every pipeline is a printed line on cream timetable paper: boxes are stops with station codes, connections are route lines with station knots, and running a box is a departure. The chrome is the signage — a deep-pine bar, a marigold signal that means "action here", and per-category line colours that do real work instead of decorating. The character is printed, not glossy. There are no gradients, no glass, no floating chrome. Type does the heavy lifting: Archivo at a signage scale for the one loud line on a screen, small uppercase labels for navigation, and IBM Plex Mono for station codes, versions, counts and timestamps. Density is high but ruled — hairlines separate, small caps label, numbers align.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper ground, pine signage shell, marigold signal, one line colour per category.
Flat surfaces and hairline rules; depth is paper, not glass.
Archivo + IBM Plex Mono; small caps labels; tabular figures.
One signature move: the route — connections read as transit lines, and selecting a box lights its route end-to-end while the rest recedes.
Status is a timetable state (running, error, stale), never a mood.

rules.name: The Line-Owns-Colour Rule
rules.body: Colour is assigned by category and by state, never by box instance. A board with twenty boxes must still read as six lines, not a rainbow.

rules.name: The Paper-Shows-Through Rule
rules.body: Areas are flat, committed colour fields at low tint so the paper ground still reads through them. They are land on the map, not cards behind cards.

rules.name: The One Loud Line Rule
rules.body: Each viewport gets exactly one large display line. Everything else is small, and the scale contrast is the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono appears only where the content is a code, a count, a version or a time. Never as a costume for "technical".

dos: Do name the category once — station dot + route colour — and let the label carry the rest.
Do keep every number in mono with tabular figures.
Do use the marigold signal for exactly one destination per screen.
Do let areas be flat colour fields at ≤12% tint so the paper shows through.
Do use the hidden legacy-glyph spans to keep the automated suite's text markers while the visible chrome stays on the icon set.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass, blurred chrome, or coloured glows.
Don't give each of the 26 box types its own hue; colour is per category and per state.
Don't put a coloured left border on a card (the old rainbow rail), or an emoji where an icon belongs — custom boxes keep the user's own emoji, which is user content.
Don't repeat a box's type in the header, the body and the footer.
Don't animate anything that doesn't signal state; no page-load choreography in the app.
